answer: An agent economy resists sybil floods by anchoring each identity to one physical device whose enclave mints a marble-hard credential: a non-transferable seal bound to that chip's fingerprint, valid a short window only. A clone farm must buy fresh silicon per head instead of replaying one key, turning mass registration into a hardware purchasing problem with a per-identity price that never falls. Honest agents grow attested history around that root, a slow nebula of verified work, while the ocean of counterfeit accounts stays weightless, since copies cannot inherit reputation earned elsewhere.
